meta.promptText: I want to buy a sunscreen that doesn't leave a white cast on Indian skin. Which one is best?

response.text:
For Indian skin tones, I’d look for a **broad-spectrum SPF 50 sunscreen with a PA++++ rating** that has a lightweight, transparent or gel-based finish. These are generally good starting points if you want to avoid a white cast, especially on medium, dusky and deeper skin tones.

The best choice also depends on whether your skin is oily, dry, acne-prone or sensitive. A sunscreen that looks invisible on one person can leave a sheen or residue on another.

search_results.title: I've switched my routine to Korean skincare - these 11 products left me GLOWING
search_results.description: A beauty expert from The Sun tested an array of Korean skincare products for over a month and reported remarkable improvements in skin hydration, clarity, and texture, leading to a glowing ‘glass skin’ effect. Korean skincare is praised for its innovative, science-backed formulations with a preventative approach to skin concerns. Eleven standout products were reviewed, including Medicube No Cast Just Glow Collagen Sunscreen (10/10 for sun protection and glow), Beauty of Joseon’s Eye Serum (9.5/10 for brightening and anti-aging), and the Medicube Night Wrapping Mask (9.5/10 for plump, hydrated skin). Other high-rated picks include SKIN1004 Centella Ampoule, Medicube Zero Pore Pads, and ANUA PDRN Hyaluronic Acid Serum, each tailored for hydration, repairing the skin barrier, and soothing inflammation. COSRX Snail Mucin, Dr Jart+ Moisturising Cream, and Mediheal Moisture Pads further impressed with their hydrating and rejuvenating effects. Products generally performed well across different skin types, including sensitive skin. The article highlights where to shop for K-beauty in the UK, emphasizing accessibility and value through retailer bundles and advent calendars. Overall, the author's switch to K-beauty resulted in improved skin health and radiance.

search_results.title: A New Sunscreen Ingredient Just Arrived in the U.S.-Here's Why Dermatologists Are Excited
search_results.description: A new sunscreen ingredient, bemotrizinol (BEMT), has been approved for use in the U.S. for the first time, marking the first such addition since the late 1990s. BEMT is a synthetic chemical filter that effectively absorbs both UVA and UVB rays without leaving a white cast, making it more cosmetically elegant than traditional mineral filters. It has been widely used in Europe and Asia but only recently gained FDA approval in the U.S. in June 2026. Dermatologists are excited because of BEMT’s photostability—it holds up well in sunlight and helps stabilize other sunscreen ingredients, enhancing overall effectiveness. Neutrogena has already incorporated BEMT into its new Cloud-Tech line, offering lightweight, invisible formulations suitable for sensitive and acne-prone skin. Dermatologist Dr. Mona Gohara highlights that a sunscreen’s feel and blendability can influence consistent use, recommending BEMT-containing products for those put off by heavy or greasy formulas. However, if you are already using and like a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher, there’s no need to switch. Regardless of the formula, reapplication every two hours and after water exposure remains essential for effective sun protection.
